filters.resolution: scan keyword/keyword.{offsets,data}.bin once; record matching keyword.id (single row expected)
scan company_name/country_code.{offsets,data}.bin in parallel with company_name/id.bin; build bitset us_company_ids[max_company_id+1]

filters.selectivity: low overall (~7-10% of title rows; episodes only)
filters.evaluation: test title.episode_nr[pos] < 100 && >= 0 on demand using id->pos

join_order.probe: movie_keyword via aux CSR on keyword_id
join_order.notes: Most selective starting point. Use indexes/movie_keyword__keyword_id__{offsets,rowids}.bin; gather distinct movie_ids into a sorted unique vector (sort + unique) for cache-friendly downstream probes.
For each candidate movie_id v, iterate [off[v], off[v+1]) on movie_companies; require at least one company_id whose us_company_bitset bit is set. Short-circuit on first match (semi-join).

join_order.build: title id->pos map (or direct id-as-position since title is sorted by id)
join_order.notes: Apply episode_nr filter; needed for MIN(t.title) projection.

join_order.build: aka_name primary CSR on person_id (presence check)
join_order.probe: cast_info primary CSR on movie_id -> person_id; for each person_id check aka_name CSR non-empty
join_order.notes: Per surviving movie_id v, iterate cast_info[ci_off[v]..ci_off[v+1]) reading person_id; for each, check aka_name [an_off[pid], an_off[pid+1]) is non-empty (an_off[pid+1] > an_off[pid]). On any match, read aka_name.name values in that range and update MIN(an.name).

data_structures.us_company_bitset: std::vector<uint64_t> sized to (max_company_id+1)/64; ~234,998 bits = ~29 KB (fits L1)
data_structures.title_id_to_pos: if title is dense PK 1..N, use identity mapping (pos = id - min_id) into a precomputed int32[max_id+2] array built by scanning title/id.bin once; size ~10 MB (fits L3)

parallelism.details: Resolve literal (serial). Build us_company_bitset and title id->pos array in parallel (independent). Enumerate movie_ids from movie_keyword aux CSR (serial, tiny). Parallelize the per-movie loop across the ~3-5k candidate movie_ids using static chunking (12 threads, chunk ~300 movies each). Each thread maintains thread-local min_name/min_title; final reduce merges 12 strings.

indexes.purpose: lookup all movie_ids for the single resolved keyword_id
per-movie company_id probe for country filter
presence check + range scan for MIN(an.name) per person_id

indexes.index: title__id__pos (pk_pos_dense, build at startup if missing)
indexes.purpose: map title.id -> row position for episode_nr filter and title text projection
n/a - we encode country filter directly as bitset over company_id

output.note: Cannot early-exit: a later row may yield a lexicographically smaller string. Must visit every qualifying row.

rationale_brief: keyword='character-name-in-title' is the most selective filter (single id => few thousand movies via movie_keyword aux CSR). Driving from this side reduces the title/cast_info/movie_companies scans to small per-movie CSR ranges, avoiding any full scan of the 36M-row cast_info or 2.6M-row movie_companies. Semi-join on company_country and presence-check on aka_name allow short-circuiting; only the MIN aggregates require reading varlen data for surviving rows.
